stem: During hepatoduodenal-ligament surgery, the surgeon identifies the portal vein and proper hepatic artery. Which duct accompanies them in the portal triad?

options.label: A
options.explanation: It joins the common hepatic duct from the gallbladder and is not the main duct of the triad.

options.label: B
options.explanation: It drains the pancreas and joins the biliary system near the duodenum, outside the portal triad.

options.label: C
options.explanation: It drains liver parenchyma directly to the inferior vena cava rather than travelling in the triad.

options.label: D
options.explanation: It accompanies the proper hepatic artery and portal vein in the hepatoduodenal ligament; the hepatic veins instead drain separately toward the inferior vena cava.

options.label: E
options.explanation: It drains the kidney and has no hepatoduodenal relationship.

context: The hepatoduodenal ligament contains the portal vein, proper hepatic artery and common bile duct. The bile duct lies anterior and to the right of the portal vein.
